ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the side length of rhombus ABCD is $6\sqrt{3}$, and point M is a moving point on diagonal AC, with $\angle ABC=120^\circ$. What is the degree measure of $\angle DAC$? What is the minimum value of $MA+MB+MD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw $ME\perp AB$ at point E and connect BD.\\
Since in rhombus ABCD, $\angle ABC=120^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle DAB=60^\circ$, $AD=AB=DC=BC$, AC perpendicularly bisects BD,\\
thus $\triangle ADB$ is an equilateral triangle, DM=BM,\\
hence $\angle DAC=\angle BAC=30^\circ$,\\
thus AM=2ME,\\
since MD=MB,\\
it follows that MA+MB+MD=2ME+2DM,\\
thus when points D, M, E are collinear, ME+DM is minimized, i.e., $MA+MB+MD$ is minimized,\\
since the side length of rhombus ABCD is $6\sqrt{3}$, $\angle DAE=60^\circ$, $\angle AED=90^\circ$,\\
it follows that AE=$\frac{1}{2}AD=3\sqrt{3}$,\\
thus DE=$\sqrt{AD^2-AE^2}=\sqrt{(6\sqrt{3})^2-(3\sqrt{3})^2}=9$,\\
hence $2DE=18$.\\
Therefore, the minimum value of $MA+MB+MD$ is $\boxed{18}$.\\
Therefore, the answer is: $\angle DAC=\boxed{30^\circ}$, the minimum value of $MA+MB+MD$ is $\boxed{18}$.
